  "findings": [
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F1",
      "proposition": "Prioritise a small pilot around quick meals and flexible replanning, with food-use and budget support as closely related tasks. Requested help is 60.8%, 59.2% and 57.1%, respectively; shared planning is 47.2%. The first three are close, so their numerical order does not establish superiority.",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/needs/values"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive task demand supporting a pilot recommendation",
      "qualification": "Eligible N/weighted N=2700/2700; answered n/weighted n/ESS=2596/2595.96/2045.54, including 116 None responses; DK=80, refusals=24. Multiple selections were allowed. The first three tasks differ by less than the 8-point attention threshold; no paired superiority test is supplied. Stated help needs do not establish digital demand.",
      "topic_cluster": "pilot_tasks"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F2",
      "proposition": "Households meeting the effort criteria are a useful recruitment audience: they report 2.19 versus 0.97 top-up days and 3.73 versus 4.93 planned-meal days per week. Differences are +1.22 days (95% CI 1.10 to 1.34) and −1.20 days (−1.36 to −1.04), both beyond the 0.5-day attention threshold.",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/need_effort/values", "analysis_results.json#/tables/NEED_EFFORT_TOPUPS/values", "analysis_results.json#/tables/NEED_EFFORT_PLANNING/values"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Prespecified external-outcome associations supported after Holm adjustment",
      "qualification": "Effort criteria are met by 31.9% of derivable cases; 154 flags are unknown. Contrast valid n=878/1588 for top-ups and 872/1586 for planning; full eligible, weighted and ESS bases are in prespecified_external_contrasts. Holm p=3.72e-84 and 3.28e-48. These are associated burdens, not effects that the pilot can be assumed to remove; the outcomes are not independent corroboration.",
      "topic_cluster": "effort_audience"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F3",
      "proposition": "Include budget and food-use problems in pilot discovery: budget-need households report overspending in at least one of four weeks at 72.3% versus 35.0%, a +37.3-point difference (95% CI 32.7 to 41.9). Waste-need households report 1.87 versus 0.87 discard days per week, a +1.00-day difference (0.87 to 1.14).",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/NEED_BUDGET_OVERSPEND/values", "analysis_results.json#/tables/NEED_WASTE_DISCARD/values"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Prespecified external-outcome associations supported after Holm adjustment",
      "qualification": "Valid n=678/1708 for overspending and 797/1664 for discard days; full bases are in prespecified_external_contrasts. Holm p=9.69e-57 and 1.04e-47. Both exceed their descriptive attention thresholds. Overspending is not a monetary amount; discard days are not quantities of food. These associations neither rank the two opportunities commercially nor estimate savings.",
      "topic_cluster": "budget_and_waste"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F4",
      "proposition": "Recruit around overlapping needs rather than exclusive personas. Effort and waste criteria coexist in 15.2% of households with both flags valid, representing 50.1% of the smaller state in that joint-valid subset. All three criteria coexist in 5.9% of households with all flags valid.",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/need_overlap/values/need_effort__need_waste", "analysis_results.json#/tables/need_combinations/values"],
      "importance": "secondary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive overlap",
      "qualification": "Pairwise valid n/weighted n/ESS=2405/2407.57/1895.59; 295 households have at least one unknown flag. Three-flag valid n/weighted n/ESS=2280/2290.14/1799.62; 420 have an unknown flag. These denominators differ. States require agreement with both defining items; failing a criterion is not proof of having no support need.",
      "topic_cluster": "audience_overlap"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F5",
      "proposition": "Keep participation optional and test the delivery format: digital-help attitudes are polarised, with 46.8% agreeing, 47.4% disagreeing and only 5.8% neutral. Strong agreement and strong disagreement each account for approximately 34.5%.",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/att_digital_help_5/values"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive distribution; no directional majority",
      "qualification": "Eligible N/weighted N=2700/2700; valid n/weighted n/ESS=2610/2609.19/2057.46; DK=67, refusals=23. Full five-category distribution is in ordinal_distributions. A near-midpoint mean conceals polarisation. Agreement is neither adoption nor willingness to pay, and disagreement does not explain which alternative format would work.",
      "topic_cluster": "delivery_format"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F6",
      "proposition": "Test setup effort, flexibility, cost and information sharing together; the barrier evidence does not identify a clear winner. Incidence is 47.9% for setup, 49.6% for rigidity, 49.6% for cost and 48.7% for privacy.",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/barriers/values"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive design constraints",
      "qualification": "Eligible N/weighted N=2700/2700; answered n/weighted n/ESS=2570/2574.37/2029.07, including 204 None responses; DK=101, refusals=29. All four estimates lie within 1.7 points, below the 8-point attention threshold. Multiple responses from users and nonusers do not identify causal adoption barriers or prove equivalence.",
      "topic_cluster": "pilot_design"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F7",
      "proposition": "Existing tools provide an important comparison for the pilot: 38.9% of valid U1 respondents report current use. Among valid current-user follow-ups, 83.2% are satisfied and 54.3% report sharing a list or plan. Investigate what additional help PantryWorks could provide before choosing a standalone tool.",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/current_tool_use/values", "analysis_results.json#/tables/tool_satisfaction_5/values", "analysis_results.json#/tables/shared_list_use_28d/values"],
      "importance": "secondary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive routed evidence informing a research question",
      "qualification": "U1 valid n/weighted n/ESS=2635/2636.34/2080.04 out of 2700 eligible. Follow-up eligibility is 1040 users, weighted N=1025.62; satisfaction valid n/weighted n/ESS=999/981.28/780.90 and sharing=996/980.23/779.91. Full satisfaction distribution and separate missing/routing counts are in analysis_claims. User satisfaction is selected and conditional; it is not all-household satisfaction, retained usage, switching intent or evidence that a new offer cannot succeed.",
      "topic_cluster": "existing_tools"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F8",
      "proposition": "Include households with children under 16 as a pilot context, without making children the sole targeting rule. They report 1.91 versus 1.17 top-up days, a +0.73-day difference (95% CI 0.63 to 0.84). Their planning difference is smaller: 4.23 versus 4.64 days, or −0.40 days (−0.54 to −0.27).",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/CHILDREN_TOPUPS/values", "analysis_results.json#/tables/CHILDREN_PLANNING/values"],
      "importance": "secondary",
      "claim_strength": "Prespecified household-context associations supported after Holm adjustment",
      "qualification": "Top-up valid n=1258/1356; planning valid n=1254/1355; full eligible, weighted and ESS bases are in prespecified_external_contrasts. Holm p=3.91e-40 and 6.64e-9. The top-up difference exceeds 0.5 days; the planning point estimate does not, although its interval includes differences larger than that threshold. Children status is not a need-state definition or an isolated causal effect.",
      "topic_cluster": "household_context"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F9",
      "proposition": "The evidence supports a focused optional pilot, not a delivery-format or commercial-impact decision. Next, compare usable delivery alternatives with households spanning effort, budget and waste needs and current-tool status; measure task completion, setup burden and repeated use. Test price acceptance separately, and use a controlled longitudinal evaluation with observed outcomes before claiming savings, purchase effects or commercial returns.",
      "evidence_refs": ["analysis_results.json#/tables/needs/values", "analysis_results.json#/tables/att_digital_help_5/values", "analysis_results.json#/tables/barriers/values", "analysis_results.json#/tables/tool_satisfaction_5/values"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Research recommendation bounded by the study design",
      "qualification": "The supplied brief describes synthetic cross-sectional self-report with no randomised concept, price test, observed purchase, revenue or longitudinal outcome. Suggested research is a next step, not evidence already collected. Task demand and significant differences cannot establish commercial value.",
      "topic_cluster": "next_evidence"
    }
  ],
  "story": {
    "beats": [
      {
        "order": 1,
        "finding_refs": ["F1"],
        "headline_intent": "Start with flexible meal support while retaining closely related food-use and budget tasks",
        "analytical_relationship": "Prioritise task scope from stated demand without declaring a statistically superior task."
      },
      {
        "order": 2,
        "finding_refs": ["F2", "F3"],
        "headline_intent": "Recruit households whose stated needs coincide with reported practical burdens",
        "analytical_relationship": "Connect need criteria to external outcomes and study-specific attention thresholds."
      },
      {
        "order": 3,
        "finding_refs": ["F4", "F8"],
        "headline_intent": "Allow overlapping needs and varied household contexts",
        "analytical_relationship": "Refine recruitment without constructing exclusive personas or using children status as a substitute for need."
      },
      {
        "order": 4,
        "finding_refs": ["F5", "F6", "F7"],
        "headline_intent": "Treat the digital format and additional value over existing tools as open questions",
        "analytical_relationship": "Qualify task demand with polarised receptivity, several similarly prevalent barriers and conditional satisfaction among existing users."
      },
      {
        "order": 5,
        "finding_refs": ["F9"],
        "headline_intent": "Use the pilot to resolve format and usage questions before testing commercial impact",
        "analytical_relationship": "Translate evidence limits into a staged research agenda."
      }
    ]
  },
  "method_notes": [
    "Only the four supplied study materials were inspected in the prompt. No tools, external sources, other files or raw respondent data were accessed. Analysis claims are rounded extracts or transparent arithmetic from supplied tables, not independently recomputed respondent-level estimates.",
    "All participants, target profiles and outcomes are synthetic. Results describe the fictional target profile, not real UK household prevalence. Relative weights sum to 2700; weighted N is an equivalent sample count, not population size.",
    "Evidence references use exact JSON Pointer paths within analysis_results.json. Analysis claims retain numerical distributions and bases; every story finding reference resolves to a finding in this object.",
    "For attitudes, codes 1–5 retain their original labels. Only A2 would be reversed when constructing planning_orientation, and only for valid responses. No index estimate is used in the narrative. DK and refusal are excluded from valid distributions, never treated as neutral.",
    "For all reported estimates, eligible and valid unweighted/weighted bases and valid Kish ESS are supplied in analysis_claims or the cited table paths. Counts of unknown flags are distinguished from observed-item DK/refusal. Display rounding can prevent percentages summing exactly to 100.",
    "The current_tool_use table begins with valid U1 cases and therefore omits screener nonresponse. Full eligibility is 2700; 2700−2635=65 have unknown U1. The supplied tables do not identify their separate DK and refusal counts, so those values remain null. U2/U3 have 1595 unasked nonusers and 65 unasked households with unknown U1; neither group is coded as dissatisfied or non-sharing.",
    "Multiple-response incidence uses answered respondents, including None rows, separately for each block; percentages may sum above 100. Joint need-state statistics use exactly the flags required by the estimate, without treating unknown flags as absence.",
    "All six required contrasts are reported using supplied fixed-weight stratified linearisation results. Holm adjustment is within exactly four needs tests and two household-context tests at alpha=0.05. Confidence intervals are normal-approximation, unadjusted 95% intervals, not simultaneous intervals. Kish ESS describes weight dispersion and is not substituted for the declared variance estimator.",
    "Inference is conditional on observed valid responses and the fixed synthetic profile. It does not remove nonresponse bias, selection into tool use or causal uncertainty. Contrasts compare each state with its complement, not overlapping states as independent groups. No additional confirmatory tests or superiority claims are made.",
    "The 0.5-day and 8-percentage-point thresholds are descriptive pilot-attention heuristics, not validated economic thresholds. B1–B3 measure days out of seven, with zero valid; they do not measure event counts, meal quantities or money.",
    "No reported headline estimate has valid n below 75 or Kish ESS below 50. Older paid-tool-user satisfaction is suppressed because valid n=18 and ESS=17.73; no estimate or ranking is reported. Other descriptive demographic tables were not selected as priority findings."
  ]
}
